posts.title: Load balancing with... Rendezvous Hashing
posts.description: About a month ago I wrote about consistent hashing . It’s a neat way for a set of nodes to agree on the placement of something without coordinating with each other. For example, a set of frontend load balancers pinning a user’s session to a particular backend server — without the need for using a component like Redis to store the information. posts.title: Perhaps Go doesn't leave atomic performance on the table after all
posts.description: In Memory ordering of atomics in Rust and Go , I described how Go and Rust differ in that Rust allows choosing from a variety of memory ordering guarantees for atomic variables, while Go has just one ordering. I ended on: And so there you go, that’s why I think this is emblematic of Rust and Go’s design choices: Rust gives you the full menu and leaves you to figure out the best for your situation,
